source: derived from the clause 4.2.1 field layout
note: The Communications Link Control Word: four octets a spacecraft sends in the operational control field of a downlink frame to report what its FARM-1 has accepted. Each vector isolates one field or flag, because the five status flags are independent bits and a decoder that treats them as an enumeration will misreport link state. Only the wire layer is here; FOP-1 and FARM-1 themselves are state machines and are not covered. Every field narrower than the type that carries it has a reject vector, because packing by shift would otherwise substitute a different value rather than refusing one.

encode.name: nominal-cop1-all-clear
encode.note: The CLCW a healthy link carries: COP-1 in effect ('01'), virtual channel 0, every flag clear, V(R) = 0. octet 0 = control word type 0<<7 | version 00<<5 | status 000<<2 | 01 = 0x01. The remaining octets are zero. This is the value a spacecraft sends before it has accepted anything.

encode.name: virtual-channel-id-max
encode.note: The VCID is 6 bits at the top of octet 1, so 63 is its maximum: octet 1 = 63<<2 = 0xfc. The two low bits are the reserved spare and stay zero.

encode.name: status-field-all-ones
encode.note: The 3-bit mission-specific status field sits above COP in effect in octet 0: 7<<2 | 01 = 0x1d. Pins that status does not bleed into the version bits above it.

encode.name: no-rf-available-flag
encode.note: The no-RF-available flag is bit 7 of octet 2, the highest of the five status flags. Set alone: octet 2 = 0x80. It says the spacecraft receiver has no carrier at all.

encode.name: no-bit-lock-flag
encode.note: The no-bit-lock flag is bit 6 of octet 2: 0x40. Carrier present but the receiver cannot recover the bit clock.

encode.name: lockout-flag
encode.note: The lockout flag is bit 5 of octet 2: 0x20. FARM-1 has locked out and will discard type-A frames until the sender recovers it, so a ground system that misreads this bit will keep transmitting into a channel that is ignoring it.

encode.name: wait-flag
encode.note: The wait flag is bit 4 of octet 2: 0x10. The spacecraft cannot accept more data for now.

encode.name: retransmit-flag
encode.note: The retransmit flag is bit 3 of octet 2: 0x08. FARM-1 is asking for a retransmission, which is what drives FOP-1 to go back.

encode.name: farm-b-counter-max
encode.note: The FARM-B counter is 2 bits at positions 2-1 of octet 2, so 3 is its maximum: 3<<1 = 0x06. Bit 0 below it is spare.

encode.name: report-value-max
encode.note: V(R), the next expected frame sequence number, is the whole of octet 3. 255 is its maximum: 0xff.

encode.name: acknowledging-the-first-frame
encode.note: The realistic case: after accepting frame 0 the spacecraft reports V(R) = 1 and every flag clear. octet 3 = 0x01. This is what carries the uplink's acknowledgement home in the operational control field of a downlink frame.

encode.name: lockout-and-retransmit-together
encode.note: Both lockout and retransmit set with V(R) = 5: octet 2 = 0x20 | 0x08 = 0x28, octet 3 = 0x05. Flags combine, so a decoder reading them as an enumeration rather than independent bits fails here.

decode.name: all-zero-octets-decode-as-a-valid-clcw
decode.note: Four zero octets are a *structurally valid* CLCW reporting V(R) = 0 with COP in effect '00'. This is why an implementation must refuse to invent an operational control field when a channel declares one but no source is supplied: a receiver cannot tell four invented zeros from a real report, so FOP-1 would believe a spacecraft was acknowledging nothing and never advance its window. The vector exists to document that a decoder must accept these octets, which is precisely what makes inventing them dangerous.

decode.name: all-fields-at-once
decode.note: Every field set to a distinct non-default value so overlapping bit reads fail here. status 5, COP-1, VCID 42, no-RF set, no-bit-lock clear, lockout set, wait clear, retransmit set, FARM-B 2, V(R) = 0x7b. octet 0 = 5<<2|1 = 0x15; octet 1 = 42<<2 = 0xa8; octet 2 = 0x80|0x20|0x08|2<<1 = 0xac; octet 3 = 0x7b.

reject.name: shorter-than-four-octets
reject.note: The CLCW is exactly four octets and occupies the whole operational control field. A decoder must not get past octet 3: the CLCW is 4 octets; the input stops after 3.

reject.name: virtual-channel-id-above-six-bit-field
reject.note: 64 does not fit the 6-bit VCID field. It must be refused rather than masked: a CLCW reports FARM-1 state for one named virtual channel, so truncating 64 to 0 would emit a control word a conforming receiver reads as reporting on VC 0, and the ground would act on the wrong channel's flags with nothing to signal the substitution.

reject.name: farm-b-counter-above-two-bit-field
reject.note: 4 does not fit the 2-bit FARM-B counter; masking it would report a count of 0.

reject.name: status-field-above-three-bit-field
reject.note: 8 does not fit the 3-bit status field; shifting it would overwrite the version bits above it.

reject.name: cop-in-effect-above-two-bit-field
reject.note: 4 does not fit the 2-bit COP-in-effect field, which sits at the bottom of octet 0.
